title: Reuse canonical service projection keys during world validation
body:
World validation repeatedly builds identical relationship-memory and story-choice keys while projecting canonical campaign states at different service locations and revisiting quest states. A Node22 CPU profile on clean published revision 88061453 attributed about 4.9 of 9.1 sampled seconds to campaign service integrity, including 1.6 seconds in canonicalCampaignServiceLocationStateKey. This is a measured follow-up to the wider suite-startup intake 63d4720207957da5; it does not complete that broader under-20-minute suite objective.

An ignored compiled-code prototype keeps a WeakMap inside one assertCampaignServiceRulesIntegrity call, caching the two location-independent key arrays per internal state object. All per-location filters, sorting, serialized keys, reachable-state enumeration, canonical evaluation limits, and active rule checks stay in place. The cache cannot survive a validation call. No cross-process validation receipt, test isolation change, or unvalidated content fast path is proposed.

Three interleaved baseline/prototype CLI pairs under the concurrent full dependency suite improved elapsed time by 17.30%, 9.07%, and 6.41%. Exact exit status, stdout, stderr, and snapshot hash matched. A separate differential execution compared every generated key with the original function and passed. The prototype was restored after the experiment; these are preliminary local timings, not full-suite speedup evidence.

Implement the scoped cache in TypeScript, independently verify that internal states cannot mutate during its lifetime, retain relationship/story predicate and cross-location validation coverage, compare output and rejection verdicts with current main, then run the required full health bar. Keep all proof limits and schema checks intact. Raw profile, paired measurements, and prototype are retained in audit-feedback-recovery/ai-runs.
